summary: Unexpected 5xx surge from streaming heartbeat mismatch and socket drift
description:
Issue summary:
Customers using long-lived streaming sessions observed a sharp increase in 5xx responses from the hosted API gateway starting ~2026-03-12 09:40 UTC. The pattern correlates with large numbers of clients that implement aggressive heartbeat/keepalive behavior (sub-30s) and intermittent TCP socket drift on edge proxies. Impact:
- LumenAI reporting 18% request error rate for streaming endpoints during the window, timed out sessions and partial responses.
- Platform-wide spike of 502/504 and some runtime OOMs in the serving fleet due to reconnect storms and connection churn.
Environment:
- Production (us-east-1), hosted API gateway fronting runtime pool (pools-03), nginx-based edge proxies + sidecar connection pool, runtime version runtime-v2.9.1.
Steps to reproduce (observed in lab with load generator):
1) Start 10k concurrent streaming clients using the LumenAI SDK configured to send JSON heartbeats every 20s.
2) Each client maintains an open HTTP/2 streaming session and occasionally sends small user messages interleaved with keepalives.
3) Introduce small packet loss / latency on proxy layer to simulate transient network jitter.
4) Observe connection resets from edge and a flurry of reconnect attempts within seconds.
Observed behavior:
- API gateway returns 502/504 for new streams as upstream runtime pool becomes partially unreachable.
- Serving runtime pods see a spike in open fds and ephemeral socket allocations, followed by OOM kills on a subset of pods.
- Edge proxy logs show `RST_STREAM` paired with `HTTP/2 PING` and long socket TIME_WAIT churn.
Expected behavior:
- Heartbeat jitter should be absorbed by connection backpressure and not cause bulk reconnect storms or upstream OOMs.
Logs / metrics pointers:
- CloudMetric: apigw.5xx.rate spike at 2026-03-12T09:40Z (dashboard link: https://dash.redwood.com/d/apigw/5xx-wave).
- Edge proxy logs (sample): "http2.RST_STREAM id=0x3fa err=2 remote=10.1.2.33" repeated.
- Runtime pod logs: "failed to accept connection: accept: too many open files" and kernel dmesg showing socket exhaustion on some nodes.
comments: 2026-03-12 10:02 - Support (Samir Patel): Initial triage with LumenAI. They confirmed they recently rolled a client SDK change that reduces heartbeat interval to 20s to keep UI ‘responsive’.
2026-03-12 11:15 - SRE (Elena Novak): Correlated apigw 5xx spike with increased TCP TIME_WAIT and high connection churn on edge proxies. Created alert rule apigw.conn-churn to track.

2026-03-12 13:40 - Support (Samir Patel): Customer applied temporary mitigation to revert SDK heartbeat to 60s; saw immediate improvement in error rate for their traffic but platform-wide noise persisted.
2026-03-13 09:30 - Runtime eng (Diego Morales): Observed file-descriptor leak in connection pool code path when stream client reconnects rapidly. Reproduced locally under synthetic reconnect storm.
2026-03-13 16:50 - PM (Aisha Kaur): Prioritizing a runtime patch to close sockets more eagerly and add backpressure at the proxy. Planning canary tomorrow.
investigation: Hypothesis 1: Aggressive client heartbeat combined with transient packet loss leads to duplicate keepalive semantics and outbound reconnect storms that exhaust FD limits on runtime nodes.
Hypothesis 2: Proxy->runtime socket handling has a small race where closed streams are not always releasing file descriptors until GC, amplifying during reconnect storms.
Metric checks: apigw.conn_attempts and apigw.conn_failures both spiked ~6x at 09:40Z. Runtime pods p63/p95 memory and open_fds increased before OOM. Node kernel shows large TIME_WAIT bucket growth.
Reproduction: In lab, reducing heartbeat to 20s + inducing 100ms packet loss caused 30% of synthetic streams to reconnect within 10s window, matching production error signature.

Temporary mitigation validated: Reverting client-side heartbeat to >=60s reduced reconnection rate by ~85% for that tenant; applying APIGW rate-limiter on new streaming session creation also damped the spike but needs cautious rollout to avoid breaking legitimate bursty UX.
resolution: Mitigation applied 2026-03-13 18:00 UTC: Enabled connection creation rate limiting on API gateway for streaming endpoints (soft limit: 200 new streams/sec per tenant) — rolled to us-east pool only. Immediate reduction in 5xx observed.

Hotfix deployed 2026-03-14 02:30 UTC to runtime (runtime-v2.9.2-hotfix): fixes a FD leak in the connection pool cleanup path and forces earlier socket close handshake when the peer resets. Canary monitored for 6 hours (no regressions).
Customer workaround: LumenAI reverted their SDK heartbeat to 60s and is publishing an SDK patch to implement exponential backoff on reconnects.

Follow-ups: 1) Full rollout of rate-limiter to other regions after load testing. 2) Backfill integration test that simulates noisy-heartbeat clients. 3) Update streaming keepalive guidance in docs. 4) Perf/QA to validate FD headroom on runtime nodes. Assigned to Diego Morales for runtime follow-up and to Nikhil Rao for APIGW policy rollout.
